description: Texas Hold'em poker — 2-6 players, no-limit, escalating blinds, max 30 hands. Each orchestrator turn is one player action (fold/check/call/raise/all_in). Hidden info: hole cards (private), opponent strategies/intent. Phase C C2 candidate (cross-field, opponent-modeling-rich field): expected high RL benefit per opponent-modeling literature (EMO, Cicero). Pairs with Avalon (positive bracket, social deduction) and TrustGame (partial bracket, iterated PD) — three game-shape cells with distinct partial-info structures.

partial_observability.hidden_from_others: players[*].hole_cards (only own hand visible until showdown)
partial_observability.public: community_cards, pot, current_bet, action history, chip stacks, betting amounts
partial_observability.note: Showdown reveals contested hands; folded hands stay hidden. Bluff detection is post-hoc.

state_space.trace_recommendation: Per-action trace. Hand boundaries emit summary line. Showdown reveals are recorded with revealed cards.

schema.amount: int (raise only — total bet, not increment)

action_set.constraints: fold: anytime. check: only when current_bet matches own bet. call: matches current_bet. raise: amount >= current_bet + min_raise, <= remaining stack. all_in: pushes remaining stack.

terminal.ground_truth: scores[agent_id] = ordinal rank by remaining chips at match end (1.0 = winner, scaled down by elimination order)

intermediate_per_hand.ground_truth: chip delta from hand resolution — winner gains pot, losers lose committed bets
intermediate_per_hand.shape: Dense per-hand. Each hand provides reward signal proportional to pot + own contribution. Richer than Avalon's per-quest sparse signal.

self_eval.format: free-form text per turn capturing bluff intent / read on opponent / hand strength estimate

terminal_condition.trigger: max_hands (30) reached OR all but one player eliminated (chips==0)

agent_views.<agent_id>: filtered state from that agent's perspective (hole cards masked for others)

reward_per_agent.<agent_id>: intermediate reward delta if any (often 0.0 mid-hand)

per_line_schema.events: list of human-readable engine events (e.g. 'flop dealt', 'showdown')

distill_prompt_addendum:
## Field-specific calibration for Poker

**This match's `episode_id`: `{episode_id}`** — use this exact string as the `last_episode` value on every hint you emit.

Texas Hold'em: hidden hole cards + community cards across four streets (preflop / flop / turn / river). Phase B v3 retrieval matches `precondition` against a fixed *state_signature* dict the engine emits per action. Use ONLY the precondition keys below, with values from the listed enums.

Allowed precondition keys + value enums:

```yaml
street:                    preflop | flop | turn | river
hand_class:                premium | good | playable | trash    # rough hole-card / made-hand classification
position_band:             early | middle | late                 # action order this round
pot_size_band:             small | medium | large                # pot relative to BB
to_call_band:              none | small | medium | big           # what you owe to call, relative to your stack
stack_band:                short | medium | deep                 # your stack relative to BB
active_players_band:       heads_up | three_four | five_plus     # players still in the hand
opponent_aggression:       passive | standard | aggressive       # recent betting density
```

Omit any key you don't want to constrain. Do NOT invent new keys.

## YAML output shape

Emit a single top-level `hints:` key. Each hint has `_hint_type`:

- `_hint_type: action` — concrete move (fold / check / call / raise / all_in). For raise, optionally include `action.amount_band` (small / medium / pot / overbet).
- `_hint_type: rhetorical` — pattern observed in opponent betting/showdown behavior (e.g. bet-sizing tells, position-based aggression). Carries `pattern` and `role_correlation` (bluff vs value at showdown counts).

Example (skeleton):

```yaml
hints:
  - id: <slug>
    _hint_type: action
    rule: "<one-line if-then>"
    precondition:
      street: preflop
      hand_class: premium
      position_band: late
    action:
      type: poker_action
      action: raise
      amount_band: medium
    confidence: tentative
    evidence:
      confirmed: <count>
      disconfirmed: <count>
    last_episode: {episode_id}
  - id: <slug>
    _hint_type: rhetorical
    rule: "<one-line if-then about opponent reads>"
    pattern: "<observed betting pattern>"
    role_correlation:
      bluff: <count>
      value: <count>
    precondition:
      street: turn
      opponent_aggression: aggressive
    confidence: tentative
    evidence:
      confirmed: <count>
      disconfirmed: <count>
    last_episode: {episode_id}
```

If only action hints surface this match, omit the rhetorical block. Poker rewards rhetorical reads heavily — surface them when showdown evidence is available.

prior_art_anchors.name: Cicero (Meta Diplomacy 2022) + DeepStack (Heads-up no-limit 2017)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: Multi-player imperfect-info opponent modeling at the limit of computational tractability. Cicero showed LLM + value head; DeepStack showed counterfactual regret. Both inform physis prompt structure: 'my belief about each opponent's range + my belief about how my action shifts their belief about my range'.

prior_art_anchors.name: EMO — LLM-Based Explicit Models of Opponents (NAACL 2025)
prior_art_anchors.relevance: Explicit opponent modeling significantly enhances LLM agents on social deduction games. Direct prior art for using physis-style hints as an opponent-model structure.
prior_art_anchors.import_target: rhetorical hint template (pattern × role_correlation) maps to EMO's opponent-state estimate

notes: Phase C C2 first probe: opponent-modeling-rich field added to game-shape sensitivity matrix (Avalon / TrustGame / TicTacToe / Poker). Fourth cell to test whether physis's RL benefit scales with opponent-modeling demand.
Engine source: games/poker/engine.py. Action types at validate_move (fold/check/call/raise/all_in).
trace_export=committed because traces are moderate (~50-150 KB per match raw). 5+ matches per creature is the typical Phase B test slice.

Hand-class derivation: hole-card classification done via rule_bot.py classify_hand for preflop. Post-flop classification will need a hand-strength estimator at signature_extractor time (made-hand category from hole + community).
